text:
kai: pushed the cross-zone A100 vs H100 run results to the shared sheet and grafana panel. quick tl;dr: H100 consistently wins on decode throughput and $/1M tokens for our 7B/13B workloads; gap narrows for 70B. link: https://go/redwood/grafana/crosszone-a100-h100

sophie: nice. can you paste the prefill vs per-token decode numbers here? we need them for capacity planning (canary pools).

kai: sure — ran across us-west2 (GCP), eu-west1 (Azure), and ap-northeast1 (AWS). configs: batch_size=1, seq_prefill=512, seq_gen=128, continuous_kv=true, kernel selection=auto with override to `fused_attn_v2` on H100 where available. quant: fp16 and int8 (GPTQ-ish) for 13B/7B.

mike: raw CSV snip from the sheet (avg of 10 runs each, median trimmed):
```
model,gpu,prefill_ms,avg_decode_ms_per_token,tokens_per_sec,cost_per_1M_usd,notes
mistral-7b,a100,540,0.9,1600,3.1,fp16
mistral-7b,h100,420,0.6,2400,2.1,fp16 + fused_attn_v2
llama2-13b,a100,980,1.8,1100,4.9,fp16
llama2-13b,h100,740,1.1,1600,3.2,fp16 + kv-cache-opt
llama2-13b,a100,int8,820,1.4,1300,3.9,quant-int8 (calib)
llama2-70b,a100,4200,8.3,140,40.2,fp16
llama2-70b,h100,3300,5.6,200,26.1,fp16 + fused-kernels
```

jen: thanks — that cost calc assumes GPU price A100=$3.5/hr, H100=$4.5/hr and amortized tokens/sec * 3600? can you share the formula you used?

kai: yep: cost_per_1M = (gpu_hourly * 3600) / (tokens_per_sec * 1e6). we also add a small infra overhead (0.95 multiplier) in the sheet for networking but numbers above are raw.

sophie: interesting that int8 on A100 brings Llama2-13B closer to H100 fp16. how stable were int8 runs? any quality regressions observed on eval set?

mike: eval pass on our 2k prompt set: int8 avg EM drop ~0.9% for 13B, perplexity +1.2. we flagged a handful of failure modes (numeric instability on long-context math), so recommend selective fallback to fp16 for those prompts.

perf-bot: automated summary: H100 median win: +45% tokens/sec on 7B/13B, +40% prefill latency improvement on average, kernel selection contributed ~12% of perf on 13B when switching to fused kernels.

mike: region notes — eu-west1 had ~8-12% worse decode latency vs us-west2 on H100 due to older PCIe gen on host (we measured memcpy stalls). ap-northeast1 was comparable to us-west2 after driver update.

sophie: for capacity sizing: if product wants 99th p50 latency <= 1200ms for a 512+128 request on llama2-13b, how many concurrent requests per H100 can we serve?

kai: rough calc: prefill (~740ms) + decode (128 * 1.1ms ~= 141ms) => ~880ms median. accounting for queuing and headroom (x1.5) => ~1.32s. so 1 H100 can sustain about floor(3600/1.32) ~= 272 sequential single-client requests/hour => roughly 272 concurrent target throughput when using continuous batching that keeps latency under SLO. better to plan 180-200 to meet 99th.

jen: actionable takeaways for ops and product?
sophie: 1) prioritize H100 for latency-sensitive canaries (7B/13B). 2) use int8 for bursty low-priority workloads — add prompt-level eval gating. 3) enforce kernel override `fused_attn_v2` rollout on H100; fallback on A100. 4) add region-level driver checks in our deploy pipeline (PCIe/pci-gen, nv_peer_mem).

mike: also add a small test to the onboarding checklist: run `perf-check --model $M --gpu {a100,h100} --seq 512 --quant {fp16,int8}` and compare tokens/sec delta; fail if >25% regression from baseline. snippet: 
```
perf-check --model llama2-13b --gpu h100 --seq 512 --batch 1 --quant fp16 --runs 10 --out csv
```

kai: I'll push the grafana panels + sheet links and tag eng-oncall and infra to review driver automation. thanks all — filing a short follow-up doc in product/evals after we vet int8 quality regressions. :white_check_mark:
